                  </ns0:note>: and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Neh. 3.25.</ns0:note> court of the prison, which <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> in the king of Judahs house <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Ieremiah</ns0:hi> was at that time a prisoner, in a prison within the Kings house. The King could keep him from revealing Gods will to the peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple, but he could not keep God from revealing himself to him. Prisons hinder us from communion with men, but often con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tribute to Gods people, freer and sweeter communion with him. In the mean time the desperate hardness of this Prince, and these peoples hearts appear, that the fear of an enemy besieg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing them could not aw them from such outragious acts of per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />secution.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 For Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">We no where read that <ns0:hi>Zedekiah</ns0:hi> immediately command<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed <ns0:hi>Ieremiah</ns0:hi> to be imprisoned, he seemeth rather to have been favourable to <ns0:hi>Ieremiah,</ns0:hi> and judicious interpreters think his pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent prison was a favourable prison, but God accounteth Princes to do that which their Ministers or subordinate Magistrates do with their connivance, and without their hinderance. Though it be wild Divinity for any to say, that inferiour Ministers or Subjects are excused by the command of the superiour, and the guilt lyeth only on them; yet it is as wild to say, they con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tract no guilt by the extravagant acts of subordinate Magistrates whom they put in place, and can punish, and remove from their places.</ns0:note>, Wherefore dost thou prophesie, and say, Thus saith the LORD, Behold I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 And Zedekiah king of Judah shall not es<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cape out of the hand of the Chaldeans, but shall surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, and shall speak with him mouth to mouth, and his eyes shall behold his eyes.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 And he shall lead Zedekiah to Babylon <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Here the cause of the Prophets imprisonment is expressed. The things were true which <ns0:hi>Ieremy</ns0:hi> prophesied, and fulfilled, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 39.5, 6, 7. and <ns0:hi>Ieremy</ns0:hi> could not forbear speaking them, because he was sent of God upon the errand, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 34.2, 3. yet the King and Court could not bear his words.</ns0:note>, and there shall he be until I visit him, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpreters are divided, whether the <ns0:hi>visitation</ns0:hi> here mentioned were a visitation of <ns0:hi>judgment,</ns0:hi> and the same with <ns0:hi>until he dye,</ns0:hi> or of <ns0:hi>mercy</ns0:hi>; it is certain <ns0:hi>Zedekiah</ns0:hi> was not put to death, only his eyes put out, and he carried into <ns0:hi>Babylon, chap.</ns0:hi> 39.7. where some think he afterward found favour with the King of <ns0:hi>Baby<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lon,</ns0:hi> certain it is that he dyed in <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> and had an honourable burial, but whether he met with any other favour, or no, the Scripture saith not; some will have the words read, <ns0:hi>until I vi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sit this people,</ns0:hi> and think that <ns0:hi>Zedekiah</ns0:hi> lived in prison in <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> till the restauration; But he was 21 years old when he began to Reign, and reigned eleven years, so as he was 32 years old when he was carried to <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36.11. and must be then 92 years old when he dyed, which is hardly probable, considering the delicate education, and life of Princes, that he
having lost his eyes, and seen so much misery, should continue 60 years longer.</ns0:note>, Though ye fight with the Chaldeans, ye shall not prosper <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Though you make many sallies out upon the <ns0:hi>Chaldeans,</ns0:hi> that are now besieging you, yet you shall be beat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />en in all, and not be able to drive them from your walls. Hi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />therto hath been but the preface to the prophetical type, and discourse in this Chapter, which now followeth.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:44" />6 ¶ And Jeremiah said, The word of the LORD came unto me, saying,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 Behold Hanameel <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">From hence may be concluded the certainty of future con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tingency in Gods eye, the coming of <ns0:hi>Hanameel,</ns0:hi> was a future contingency, yet certainly known to God, so as he could tell the Prophet he would come.</ns0:note> the son of Shallum thine uncle, shall come unto thee, saying, Buy thee my field that <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> in Anathoth <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Anathoth</ns0:hi> (as appears from <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 21.18.) was one of the Cities of the <ns0:hi>Levites</ns0:hi>; hence a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riseth a question, how it could be sold to <ns0:hi>Ieremiah,</ns0:hi> who by the Law might not possess it, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 18.20. being a <ns0:hi>Levite.</ns0:hi> Some excuse it from the command of God, who might dispense with his own Law, but this seemeth not enough, because it is said afterward, <ns0:hi>The right of Redemption is thine.</ns0:hi> 2. Others therefore say the <ns0:hi>Levites</ns0:hi> might have some small possessions, though no plowed land: They might have Houses, and Orchards, and Gardens, in Cities and Suburbs. But that these might be sold seemeth contrary to the Law, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 25.34. It is therefore rather thought to be meant of some small estate lest to <ns0:hi>Ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nameel</ns0:hi> from his Ancestors.</ns0:note>, for the right of re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />demption <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> thine to buy <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">The right of <ns0:hi>Redemption</ns0:hi> belonged to the next of Kin, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 25.25. <ns0:hi>Ruth</ns0:hi> 4.4.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 So Hanameel my uncles son came to me in the court of the prison, according to the word of the LORD <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Hanameel</ns0:hi> came <ns0:hi>freely,</ns0:hi> none drave, or forced him, yet he came <ns0:hi>necessarily</ns0:hi> as to the <ns0:hi>event,</ns0:hi> he could not but go, else God had not told the Prophet truth.</ns0:note>, and said unto me, Buy my field, I pray thee, that <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> in Anathoth, which <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> in the country of Benjamin, for the right of inheri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tance <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> thine, and the redemption <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> thine, buy <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> for thy self: then I knew that this <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> the word of the LORD <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">When I saw it came to pass, knowing that God alone knew what was in mens hearts, and what they would do: I knew my former mentioned Reve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lation was from God.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 And I bought the field of Hanameel my un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cles son, that <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> in Anathoth, and weighed him the money, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>seven she<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />kels, and ten</ns0:hi> pieces <ns0:hi>of silver.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> seventeen shekels of silver <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">That is, about 2. <ns0:hi>l.</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>s.</ns0:hi> 6 <ns0:hi>d.</ns0:hi> a small purchase, which ar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gues the field here mentioned to be but some <ns0:hi>Orchard</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Garden,</ns0:hi> though we must allow the price of Land strangely fallen at this time, when the Enemy was besieging the chief City of the Country. It should seem they were wont there to make their payments, more by weight, then by tale.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And I <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>wrote in the book.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> subscribed the evidence, and seal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> and took witnesses, and weighed <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> the money in the ballances <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">I went through with the purchase, setting my hand to, and sealing the deed, and taking witnesses to it, (as is usual.)</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 So I took the evidence of the purchase, <ns0:hi>both that which was</ns0:hi> sealed <ns0:hi>according</ns0:hi> to the law and custom, and <ns0:hi>that which was</ns0:hi> open <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">It is most probable, that upon such bargains and sales a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> two instruments were made, the one sealed up, to be kept by the purchaser, the other open, to be shewed to the Judges, and by them ratified, and that this was the law and custom ordinarily amongst the <ns0:hi>Jews</ns0:hi> upon purchases; both which <ns0:hi>Ieremy</ns0:hi> kept, the one for his use, the other to produce in Court for Ratification. There is no certainty in the guesses that some others make, why there were two Copyes: Nothing appeareth but that the Prophet bought this little purchase with the same rites and circumstances that men ordinarily in that Country made purchases in times of peace, and civil order.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And I gave the evidence of the purchase un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Maa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />seiah <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">This <ns0:hi>Baruch</ns0:hi> (as appeareth from <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 36.4, 26.) was a Scribe, and an attendant upon <ns0:hi>Ieremiah,</ns0:hi> and one who wrote things for him, and from his mouth.</ns0:note>, in the sight of Hanameel my uncles <ns0:hi>son,</ns0:hi> and in the presence of the <ns0:note place="margin">See Isa. 8.2.</ns0:note> witnesses, that sub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scribed the book of the purchase, before all the Jews that sate in the court of the prison <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">He made this purchase with all the usual formalities, to make it publick, he signed and sealed it before witnesses, and delivered it to <ns0:hi>Baruch,</ns0:hi> to keep in the presence of them all, and in the presence of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> who casually were in the place when the thing was done.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 ¶ And I charged Baruch before them, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 Thus saith the LORD of hosts the God of Israel, Take these evidences, this evidence of the purchase, both <ns0:hi>which is</ns0:hi> sealed, and this evidence <ns0:hi>which is</ns0:hi> open, and put them in an earthen ves<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sel, that they may continue many days.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 For thus saith the LORD of hosts the God of Israel, Houses and fields, and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Here is nothing of any seeming difficulty in these verses, but only why the Prophet commandeth <ns0:hi>Baruch</ns0:hi> to put the evi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dences in an <ns0:hi>Ea<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>then Vessel,</ns0:hi> wh<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ch himself also expounds, that they might continue many dayes that is not defaced, had they been hid many dayes in the Earth, they would have been rotten, had they been above ground in a Box or Chest, they might have been lost, or taken away by the Souldiers plun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dering houses, or at least burnt with fire. <ns0:hi>Verse</ns0:hi> 15. The Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet expounds Gods meaning in this command to him, and his own design, in so formal a buying of so small a purchase, especially considering, that, very probably, <ns0:hi>Ieremiah</ns0:hi> was no great purchaser, nor very greedy of purchases; he lets them know that all this was for a sign of the truth of what God had revealed to him concerning the peoples return, though after many days, (sixty years from this time) and also of the firm assent he gave to that divine Revelation, That purchases should one day be injoyed again in <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> and houses, fields, and vineyards in it, should be again possessed.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 ¶ Now when I had delivered the evidence of the purchase unto Baruch the son of Neriah, <ns0:hi>I</ns0:hi> prayed unto the Lord, saying <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">What he prayed for; the matter of his prayer in the follow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing verses will inform us, but it should seem by it, that he was not without his perplexities, though he yielded an absolute o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bedie<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ce to Gods command, yet he prayeth for a clearer re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />velation of his meaning in this thing.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Ah Lord GOD, behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> there is <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 18.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> verse 27. Luke 1.3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> nothing <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>hid <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> thee.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> too hard for thee <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">He beginneth his prayer with a recognition of Gods om<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nipotency, and the infiniteness of his power, which was shewed in his first making the Heaven and the Earth, as we read, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 1. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 146.6. God himself used this instance to con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />firm his peoples faith in his ability to do what he pleased, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 27.5. It is observable that the servants of God in Holy Writ, used in their Prayers to give God such names, as might help to confirm their Faith as to what they asked. Nothing can fur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther be necessary to confirm our Faith that we shall have what we ask; then for us to be perswaded that the person is <ns0:hi>able</ns0:hi> to do it, and also willing. The prophet beginneth with a de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />claration of his faith in God as to the first, then goes on to the second.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 Thou shewest loving kindness unto thou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sands, and recompensest the iniquity of the fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers into the bosom of their children after them <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">This is the name which God gave himself, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 34.7. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 5.9, 10. and of this latter clause declarative of the ven<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />geance of God in punishing children for their Parents sins, are many instances in Scripture. <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 7.24. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 2.33, 34. 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 14.10, 11. and 21.24.</ns0:note>, the great, the mighty God, the LORD of hosts <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> his name.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Great in counsel <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Who dost nothing but in infinite wisdom, as if thou hadst taken counsel upon it, and art mighty in thy works of Provi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence, by which thou governest the world.</ns0:note>, and mighty in work <ns0:hi>y,</ns0:hi> (for thine <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Job 34.21. Psal. 33.13. Prov. 5.21. chap. 16.17.</ns0:note> eyes <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> open upon all the wayes of the sons of men <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 17.10.</ns0:note>, to give every one according to his wayes, and according to the fruit of his doings <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Whose eyes run to and fro the Earth, beholding the evil and the good, so that all things are naked before thee, and art not a meer curi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous and idle spectator of mens actions, but lookest upon them for that end, that thou mightest reward or punish them, ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cordingly as thou seest their actions good, or bad in thy sight.</ns0:note>.)</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 Which hast set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> unto this day <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Who didst wonders of justice in the Land of <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> such as are remembred and made matters of astonishing discour<ns0:gap reason="illegible: missing" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e even to this day,</ns0:note>, and in Is<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rael <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">and wroughtest wonders of mercy in <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> bringing them out of <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> through the Red Sea, raining them down <ns0:hi>Manna</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Quails</ns0:hi> from heaven, and fetching water out of the rock for them, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and amongst <ns0:hi>other</ns0:hi> men <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">And hast done also many wond<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rous works in other places, by which thou hast made thy self a Glorious Name.</ns0:note>, and hast made thee a name as at this day.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:44" />And hast brought forth thy people Israel, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 6.6. 2 Sam. 7.23. 1 Chron. 17.21</ns0:note> out of the land of Egypt with signs, and with wonders, and with a strong hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with great terror <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The History of this we have in the 11 or 12 first Chapters of <ns0:hi>Exodus,</ns0:hi> God sent 10 plagues upon <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> one after another, before <ns0:hi>Pharaoh</ns0:hi> would let them go, and when he pursued after them, divided the Red Sea for them, that they might pass through, and then brought the Waters back upon the <ns0:hi>Egypti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ans,</ns0:hi> pursuing after them, through the Sea.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And hast given them this land which thou didst swear unto their Fathers to give them <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">God owneth this Oath, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 6.8.</ns0:note> a land flowing with milk and hony <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">That is, abounding with all necessary things, and all pleasant things. <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi> is of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ten thus described, <ns0:hi>Exod</ns0:hi> 3.8, 17, and 13.5. and 33.3 <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 20.24. <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 14.8. and 16.13, 14. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 6.3. and 11.9, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 And they came in and possessed it <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">In <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>he former passage he acknowledged Gods goodness<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> here he owns his Truth and Faithfulness, so conducting this People by his Providence, that they came into the promised Land and possessed it.</ns0:note>, but they obeyed not thy voice, neither walked in thy law <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Having acknowledged Gods Power, Omniscience, Goodness, Truth and Faithfulness, he comes to own his Justice, confessing that this People for whom God had done so much, had very ill requited him, not <ns0:hi>obeying his voice,</ns0:hi> which he expounds by <ns0:hi>not walking in his law</ns0:hi>; for the Law was Gods voice to them.</ns0:note>, they have done nothing at all that thou commandedst them to do <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">This he aggravateth by saying they had done nothing of what he had commanded, not breaking some particular Law, but the whole Law of God.</ns0:note>: there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore thou hast caused all this evil to come upon them <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Therefore God was righteous in bringing this Sword, Pestilence and Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mine upon them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Behold the <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>Engines of <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>hot.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> mounts <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">The word signifies <ns0:hi>Ramparts,</ns0:hi> or rather <ns0:hi>battering Rams,</ns0:hi> En<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gines of W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r which those Nations used to batter Walls, or to shoot great stones into places besieged.</ns0:note>, they are come unto the city to take it <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">They are already Besieging <ns0:hi>Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> and have been for some time.</ns0:note>, and the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans, that fight a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst it <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">And the City is even ready to be taken and cannot hold out.</ns0:note>, because of the sword, and of the fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mine, and of the pestilence <ns0:note n="u" place="margin">So many daily are killed, either with the Sword of the Enemy, or by Famine for want of provision, or by the Pestilence.</ns0:note>, and what thou hast spoken is come to pass <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Thou art just, and righteous in all this, and hast done but according to what thou thr<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>atnedst to do, to a sinful people that would not obey thy voice.</ns0:note>, and behold, thou seest <ns0:hi>it.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 And thou hast said unto me, O Lord GOD; Buy thee the field for money, and take witnesses: <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>though</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> for the city is given into the hands of the Chaldeans <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">In this Verse again the particle <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.13.</ns0:note> upon whose roofs they have offered incense unto Baal, and poured out drink-offerings unto other Gods to provoke me to anger <ns0:hi>a.</ns0:hi>
                  <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">But in this execution of my vengeance I shall not act by prerogative, but as a just and righteous judge, vindicating the violation of my laws, they have polluted their hou<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">

               <ns0:p n="30">30 For the children of Israel, and the children of Judah have only done evil before me from their youth: for the children of Israel, have only pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />voked me to anger with the works of their hands, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">If they had offended me only by some particular single acts, or by some few omissions, or but for a small time; I might have been judged too severe upon them, but from the time they first began to be a Nation, they have made it their business, course, and trade, passing from one Idolatry to another, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 For this city hath been to me <ns0:hi>as</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>for my anger.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> a pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vocation of mine anger, and of my fury, from the day that they built it, even to this day <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Solomon</ns0:hi> finished the Building of <ns0:hi>Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> and he at least suffered Idolatry in it, 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 11.4.8. People have alwayes been so fond of <ns0:hi>worshipping God</ns0:hi> according to their own fancies and inventions, that even in <ns0:hi>I<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>dah</ns0:hi> (except in <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s time) the worship of God could hardly be preserved pure, during the entire Reign of one King.</ns0:note>, that I should remove it from before my face <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">As if they had done it on purpose to provoke me to destroy the City, and cast the people of it out. Nothing more easie than for people to keep close to the Divine Rule; as to External Acts in Worship, nothing is more provocative of God that their doing the contrary. Yet nothing hath been more rarely done in any Nation, as if men had set themselves to dare a jealous God.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 Because of all the evil of the children of Is<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rael, and of the children of Judah which they have done, to provoke me to anger, they, their kings, their princes, their priests, and their prophets, and the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Je<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rusalem <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Still God maketh their destruction to be of themselves, as the meritorious cause, provoking him to that wrath he executed upon them. The whole head was sick, the whole heart faint. All orders of men were corrupted, so as there was no hope of their Reformation, or growing better.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 And they have turned unto me the <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>

                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>

Ezek. 8.5, 16.</ns0:note> set their abominations <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Their Idols, which above all things the jealous God abhor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />reth, and therefore he calleth them <ns0:hi>abominations</ns0:hi> in the abstract for abominable things, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 32.16, 1 <ns0:hi>Ki gs</ns0:hi> 11.5. 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 23.13.</ns0:note> in the house which is called by my name to defile it <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">That is, <ns0:hi>in the Temple,</ns0:hi> which was ordinarily called the House of the Lord, and the Temple of the Lord.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:45" />35 And they built the high places of Baal which <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 7.31.19.5.</ns0:note> cause their sons and their daughters to pass through <ns0:hi>the fire</ns0:hi> unto <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 18.21.</ns0:note> Molech, which I com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manded them not, neither came it into my mind that they should do this abomination to cause Ju<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dah to sin <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">See the notes on <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 19.5, 6. where all passages we meet with here are fully opened.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 ¶ And now therefore thus saith the LORD the God of Israel, concerning this city, whereof ye say, It shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, by the sword, and by the fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mine, and by the pestilence <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">The Jews now began to see that the <ns0:hi>Chaldeans</ns0:hi> would take the City, and to be as dead hearted as before they were full of courage, and to give over themselves for ever as lost.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 Behold, I will <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.3. chap 23.3. and 29.14. and 31.10.</ns0:note> gather them out of all countreys, whither I have driven them in mine anger, and in my fury, and in great wrath: and I will bring them again unto this place, and I will cause them to dwell safely <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Though the City shall be taken and you shall go into Cap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tivity, yet you shall not be utterly lost<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> I will gather you again, and you shall have as quiet an habitation as ever.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 And they shall be <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 24.7. and 30.22. and 31.33.</ns0:note> my people, and I will be their God <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">I will renew my Covenant with them, and keep my Cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nant towards them, they shall serve me more faithfully, and I will own them and take care of them, and bless them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 And I will give them <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezek. 11.19.</ns0:note> one heart <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">I will give them union and concord<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or an onene<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> mind, and judgment; as to the thing<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> of God, they shall not be some for superstitious and idolatrous Worship, and some for my true Worship.</ns0:note>, and one way <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">They shall all Worship me according to the rule I have given them.</ns0:note>, that they may fear me for <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>all days.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> ever <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">That they may Worship me in Truth, as a people that have a dread of me upon their hearts.</ns0:note>, for the good of them, and of their children after them <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">This will be for the profit both of them, and their posterity, many dayes, even so long as they shall continue so to do.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 31.31.</ns0:note> I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>from a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                        <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> from them to do them good <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">This promise manifestly r<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>lateth to those Jews that should receive the Lord Jesus Christ o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> that were <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> indeed; for as to others, God did turn away from doing them good, when their City was taken by <ns0:hi>Titus</ns0:hi>; unless it be to be understood of a national conversion of the Jews, not yet effected.</ns0:note>, but I will put my fear into their hearts, that they shall not depart from me <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">My spirit which shall beget in them a dread of me, so as they shall not depart from me, Hence some conclude well that when once the body of the Jews shall be converted, they shall never again apos<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>atize from God. It may well from hence be concluded that both <ns0:hi>Conversion</ns0:hi> unto God, and perseverance in the wayes of God are the gifts of God, we are kept <ns0:hi>by the power of God, through faith unto Salvation.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 Yea, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Zeph. 3.12.</ns0:note> I will rejoice over them, to do them good <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">I will not onely do them good, but I will take pleasure, and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">

                        </ns0:gap>ility.</ns0:hi>

               <ns0:p n="42">42 For thus saith the LORD, Like as I have brought all this great evil upon this people, so will I bring upon them all the good that I have promised them <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">You shall find me as true to my promises, as you have found me to my threatnings.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
